title: Minimally $(k,k)$-edge-connected graphs via spectral radius
summary: For $l > 1$, the $l$-edge-connectivity $κ'_l(G)$ of a connected graph $G$ is defined as the minimum number of edges whose removal leaves a graph with at least $l$ components. A graph is minimally $(k,l)$-edge-connected if $κ'_l(G)\geq k$ but for any edge $e\in E(G)$ satisfies that $κ'_l(G-e)< k$. Motivated by two foundational extremal problems: Brualdi and Solheid's problem [SIAM J.
